chunks: And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn al-Ziyad, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a woman whose husband died while they had not yet consummated the marriage, he said: 'She does not marry until she completes a waiting period of four months and ten days, which is the waiting period for one whose husband has died.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.وَلَمْ يَمَسَّهَا: And he did not touch her (not consummated)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a widow whose husband died before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* records Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib’s ruling that a widow whose marriage was not yet consummated observes the same waiting period (iddah) of four months and ten days as one whose marriage was consummated. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it clarifies that the distinction in iddah duration applies primarily to divorce versus death, rather than consummation status in the case of a husband's death. It underscores the consistency of the Quranic prescription for widows regardless of marital intimacy.
